new_value: • Kosa refers to a treasury or repository of wealth (part of the Saptanga theory of statecraft described in Kautilya's Arthashastra), making it an administrative/economic term rather than a kinship term. • Kula, Vamsa, and Gotra all belong to the category of social and familial organization: • Option A (Kula): Refers to the family or household unit in ancient Indian social structures. • Option B (Vamsa): Refers to a lineage, genealogy, or dynasty traced through successive generations. • Option D (Gotra): Refers to an exogamous clan lineage traced back to a common mythical Vedic seer (rishi). • Often confused with: Kosa (treasury/wealth) vs. Kosha (sheaths of the Atman in Vedanta philosophy, such as Annamaya Kosha), though both are entirely distinct from the kinship terms Kula, Vamsa, and Gotra.
